statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-106072 is a Node.js TLS hostname-verification flaw: a certificate with only a DNS SAN can authenticate an IP endpoint when the client connects with a non-canonical IPv4 spelling such as 0177.0.0.1, 0x7f.0.0.1, 2130706433 or 127.1. Node.js's CVE record lists 22.x as affected through 22.23.3, and the 2026-10-21 security release (https://nodejs.org/en/blog/vulnerability/october-2026-security-releases) names 22.x among the fixed lines. Node.js's v22 changelog attributes the 22.x fix to commit d7663560ac, 'tls: reject non-canonical IP addresses' (https://github.com/nodejs/node/commit/d7663560ac), released in 22.23.4; the changelog on Node.js's main branch now lists that commit under both CVE-2026-106069 and CVE-2026-106072 (https://github.com/nodejs/node/commit/f145fa4692). With it, tls.checkServerIdentity() in lib/tls.js rejects any host that becomes an IP address only after domainToASCII() normalization, and the regression test added with it checks each spelling above against a certificate whose only SAN is DNS:127.0.0.1. We read the node binary in every published DHI nodejs-22 package for Alpine 3.23 on x86_64 and aarch64: 22.23.4-r0 is the first that reports Node.js v22.23.4 and contains that 'Host is a non-canonical IP address' rejection; 22.22.0-r0 through 22.23.3-r0 report Node.js 22.22.0 through 22.23.3 and lack it. We called tls.checkServerIdentity() with each spelling and that certificate on the aarch64 builds: 22.23.4-r0 rejects all four as non-canonical IP addresses. The earlier builds we ran (22.22.0-r0, 22.22.3-r0, 22.23.0-r0 and 22.23.3-r0) reject them too, because 22.22.x does not normalize the host and 22.23.0 to 22.23.3 match the normalized address only against IP Address SANs; the change that would have matched such hosts against DNS names (commit beb4cd4cd3, https://github.com/nodejs/node/commit/beb4cd4cd3) first shipped in 22.23.4 together with this fix. This decision follows Node.js's record and marks 22.23.4-r0 as the first fixed build.
